title: ENG-205 Sir Gawain Part 1 — 3 Numbers & Dates
subject: ENG-205

cards.def: Camelot's Christmas feasting lasts a full fortnight and one day before the New Year challenge.
The Green Knight promises twelve months of peace, then claims the return blow in one year and one day.
The first of the pentangle's five fives is that Gawain was deemed flawless in his five senses.
The second of the pentangle's five fives is that Gawain's five fingers were never at fault.
The third of the pentangle's five fives is that Gawain's faith was founded in the five wounds Christ received on the cross.
The fourth of the pentangle's five fives is the fortitude Gawain found in the five joys Mary conceived in her son: Annunciation, Nativity, Resurrection, Ascension, and Assumption.
The fifth set of five is friendship and fraternity with fellow men, purity and politeness that impressed at all times, and pity, which surpassed all pointedness.

cards.term: Fully faithful in five ways five times over
cards.def: Armitage's summary of why the pentangle suits Gawain: he is fully faithful in five ways five times over.
At Michaelmas the moon stands as that season's sign, a warning to Gawain to rouse himself and ride.
Gawain stayed until All Saints' Day by Arthur's side before asking leave to set out for the return blow.
Gawain must face the Green Chapel knight as dawn on New Year's Day draws near.

cards.term: Two miles to the Green Chapel
cards.def: Bertilak tells Gawain the Green Chapel is near, two miles at most away, so Gawain can stay until New Year's morning.
Sir Gawain belongs to the alliterative revival in Middle English of the fourteenth century.
By the time of Sir Gawain, the romance tradition developed in France was already over three hundred years old.

cards.term: PPT names for Gawain's five virtues
cards.def: The instructor PowerPoint lists Gawain's five virtues as boundless beneficence, brotherly love, pure mind, manners, and compassion.
